identity: Wageningen University & Research, English-taught Bachelor Earth System Sciences (BSW,56968), renamed from Soil, Water, Atmosphere; generic target without a named academic track; current2026–2027 handbook.
components: The programme also includes non-credit personal development across three years. General, laboratory and fieldwork safety training applies to the relevant practical activities; these requirements are not extra EC.

WUR studies atmospheric thermodynamics, radiation, cloud physics, chemistry and dynamics quantitatively. UCR’s Climate Change course addresses greenhouse forcing, feedbacks and impacts, without the same dedicated atmospheric-physics sequence.
This example uses Mathematics Applied: Introduction for students with VWO Mathematics A. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead; the choice follows prior preparation and study advice.
System Earth: Climate and Global Change
Chemical Processes in Soil, Water, Atmosphere

WUR explicitly models soil–vegetation–atmosphere exchanges, evapotranspiration, radiation and transport. General ecological energy and matter cycles at UCR do not reproduce that coupled physical sequence.
Geology, Soils and Landscapes of the Northwest European Lowlands

One of three selected advanced options. This course combines aquifer systems, groundwater modelling and field investigation. It assumes earlier water-analysis and water-quantity/quality study and requires fieldwork safety.
One of three selected advanced options. This course develops Python programming for scientific data work; it assumes elementary computer skills.
Sedimentary Geology of Lowlands: Principles, Methods and Applications

One of three selected advanced options. This course studies sedimentary successions and lowland stratigraphy through field and laboratory methods. It builds on the common geology course and requires laboratory and fieldwork safety.
The illustrated pathway preserves 30 EC for a minor and/or individually chosen electives. Optional data-science courses or a named minor are not made compulsory.

The required 12 EC thesis is individual Earth-system research. Entry requires at least 102 EC of compulsory and restricted courses, all 60 first-year EC, and the first two years of personal-development assignments or an agreed subset. Supervisors may specify prior-course knowledge for a topic. UCR’s optional 15 EC independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 EC.

findings: The current official programme page and BSW2026 handbook establish exact identity, English instruction, Earth-crust/surface/atmosphere and soil-water-biosphere interactions, physical/chemical/biological mechanisms, quantitative modelling and extensive field/lab practicals. Renaming is verified; historical name is retained internally rather than in the display heading.

CP-CC requires117credited EC. Its positive-credit units include57EC in B1 and60EC in B2; zero-credit safety and personal development are separate. CP-RO01 requires3EC based on prior preparation: VWO MathematicsA selects MAT14803; MathematicsB selects Statistics1 MAT15303. Thus B1=60EC with the illustrated MathematicsA preparation. It is not an arbitrary official-order choice.

CP-RO02 requires18EC from17listed6EC advanced choices. The generic target names no route and none is fabricated. Retain the first three in official order: Hydrogeology, Programming inPython and SedimentaryGeology. Their common-course assumed knowledge and mandatory safety are available in the illustrated prior programme. The noncompulsory data-science cluster has0minimum credits and is not added by default.

CP-THESIS/YWU81312 supplies12EC individual Earth-system research. Mandatory entry is102EC compulsory/restricted including all60B1 plus completed first-two-year YWU00300 assignments or coordinator-agreed subset. By completing the120EC first-two-year package and18EC advanced choices, the illustrated path satisfies the numerical preparation; the PDP condition is recorded separately, not invented credits. Topic-specific supervisor assumptions are communicated when topics are announced.

Thesis content includes proposal, research with field/lab/modelling or existing data, written thesis, symposium presentation, oral supervisor discussion and ethical reflection. Topic allocation has May/November cycles; later eligible students can be allocated subsequently. A six-month completion condition applies when delay is not due to planned activities or force majeure. No group sustainability course is treated as its equivalent.

General/lab/field safety modules and YWU00300 carry0EC. Mandatory practical-safety conditions are explicit in the selected chemistry, geology, ecology, water and advanced field modules. Current course assumptions sometimes use older Mathematics2/3 or Water2 labels; these are distinguished from MandatoryKnowledge fields and read in the current prescribed sequence, not invented as additional absent compulsory units.

ELECTIVES genuinely completes the degree to180EC. After117+3+18+12=150, retain30EC for a minor/individual electives. Public examples DisasterRiskAndResilience and Geo-informationForEnvironmentAndSociety are optional minors; Soil/Water/Atmosphere describe study domains, not additional compulsory tracks. No teacher-qualification route or elective package is asserted for the illustrated path.

The September2025 PDF remains historical orientation. Current2026 programme/module facts control the complete coherent pathway. No unresolved essential source conflict remains and no redundant OER search or university contact is required.
